subject: groupComparison using multiple conditions to compare against each other?

messages.author: f269294f1996b292
messages.subject: groupComparison using multiple conditions to compare against each other?
parts:
Dear MSStats-Team,

I am currently using MSStats for some DIA data analysis and I was wondering if and how the groupComparison function would be able to handle comparisons using multiple conditions:

E.g. the Conditions are
Ctrl        Subtype1_Sample1             Subtype 2_Sample1            Subtype1_Sample2         Subtype2_Sample2

Would it be possible to do a comparison investigating the two Subtypes like this:

comparison <- matrix(c(0,1,-1,1,-1),nrow=1)

Would this combine Sample1 and Sample2 for Subtype1 and compare it against both samples for Subtype2???


Best regards and many thanks for any help regardiong this question
Matthias

messages.author: b0c55e3f9d535cb8
messages.subject: Re: groupComparison using multiple conditions to compare against each other?
parts:
Dear Matthias,

Have you figured out what you want? I am having a similar experimental design and based on your question. wanted to know if there are any interactions, I got the following response from Dr. Vitek. 

"The interaction is encoded in the MSstats model directly. When you have 2 factors with 2 levels each, we in fact fit a model with 1 factor and 4 levels (i.e. all combinations of the original levels). This is equivalent to fitting a model with two factors and their interaction.

If you would like to test the hypothesis that the two factors are additive (i.e., their interaction is zero), you need to specify a particular contrast, after the model fit. If I denote Condition(1,1) the first level of the first factor and the first level of the second factor, etc, testing for the interaction being zero is equivalent to testing Condition(1,1) - Condition(1,2) - Condition(2,1) + Condition(2,2) = 0  You can specify this in the contrast function."

"You will need to specify
Comparison5 <- matrix(c(...),nrow=1)
And replace … with c(1,-1, -1,1), except that you need to change the order of the coefficients such that they correspond to Condition(1,1) - Condition(1,2) - Condition(2,1) + Condition(2,2) (I cannot do it for you since I do not know how your factors are coded)."

Hope this helps!

Priya
